newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel works council gives ultimatium over sick pay.
newsitem.headline: Opel works council gives ultimatium over sick pay.

text.p: The works council at Adam Opel AG will not approve overtime shifts at the German carmaker if Opel does not reverse its new policy on sick-pay benefits by next Tuesday, a newspaper reported on Thursday.

The Westdeutschen Allgemeinen Zeitung said works council president Peter Jaszczyk said the ultimatum has been delivered to the management board at Opel, a unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, and could spread to foreign units of Opel.

Beginning November 1, Opel said it would implement a controversial new law that calls for workers to receive 80 percent of gross wages for sick days compared to the prior 100 percent. Opel said it has been negotiating with its unions.
An Opel spokesman could not be reached for comment on Thursday since the company was closed for a national holiday.

Labour unions across Germany have protested the new law with widespread demonstrations and strikes against a number of major companies, including Daimler-Benz AG, that have implemented the new policy.

Jaszczyk also said overtime hours have already been cut in the car parts production areas at Opel, which would weaken Opel's ability to produce cars under its "just-in-time" production planning for parts.
"As of Friday at 1400 local time, there will be no more cars produced" at the major Opel plant in Bochum, he said, noting each shift not worked costs Opel about 500 cars.
